unit_label: BRBL B U06: Securities and modes of charge II — Distinguish ordinary pledge retainer, extraordinary expenses and unrelated debts

facts.locator: printed pp. 202–204; PDF page = printed page + 19
facts.statement: Courseware separates pledge interest/preservation costs, extraordinary expenses, subsequent advances and reasonable care precautions.

facts.locator: sections 151–152, PDF p. 39; sections 173–175, PDF p. 42
facts.statement: Section 173 retainer includes the secured debt/promise, interest and necessary possession/preservation expenses. Section 174 restricts retention for other debts absent a contract, with the stated presumption for subsequent advances unless contrary terms. Section 175 gives a right to receive extraordinary preservation expenses. Bailment care follows the ordinary-prudence standard with section 152 qualification.

payload.title: Identify why each retained amount is secured
payload.core_explanation_md:
Section 173 covers retention for the secured obligation, interest and necessary expenses of possession or preservation. A review should match each claimed amount to its legal or contractual basis. An unrelated debt should not be silently added just because the bank already holds the goods.

Section 174 supplies the other-debt qualification and a distinct presumption concerning subsequent advances, subject to anything contrary. Record relevant contract terms and the timing of advances. The useful question is not whether the customer owes anything at all, but whether this retention covers the particular amount under the applicable rule.

self_check.prompt_text: Why is a separate unrelated debt not automatically included merely because the bank has possession?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Section 174 requires the relevant contract basis, subject to its qualified subsequent-advance presumption.

payload.title: Expense recovery and permission to retain are different
payload.core_explanation_md:
Section 175 entitles the pawnee to receive extraordinary expenses incurred for preservation. Distinguish that recovery entitlement from section 173 retention for necessary possession or preservation expenses. Do not assume every extraordinary invoice automatically supplies the same statutory retention power without reviewing the governing terms and rule.

The bank also owes care as bailee. Under section 151, compare its conduct with what an ordinarily prudent person would do for goods of the same bulk, quality and value in similar circumstances. Section 152 qualifies responsibility where the required care is taken and no special contract applies. Insurance and a warehouse receipt do not replace a reasoned custody and care plan.

self_check.prompt_text: Does the existence of insurance itself establish that the bank exercised the required bailment care?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The statutory care standard concerns the bank conduct in the circumstances.

payload.stem_md: A pawnee relies only on section 175 to claim that any extraordinary preservation expenditure automatically has the identical statutory retainer treatment as section 173 necessary expenses. What distinction is missing?

options.text_md: A right to receive extraordinary expenses must be distinguished from the stated retainer rights and any contractual basis
options.explanation_md: The provisions describe distinct rights; their statutory wording should not be collapsed into one universal retention rule.

options.text_md: Extraordinary preservation expenses are never recoverable
options.explanation_md: Section 175 expressly recognises an entitlement to receive them.

options.text_md: Necessary possession expenses can never be relevant to retention
options.explanation_md: Section 173 expressly includes necessary possession/preservation expenses.

options.text_md: All customer debts automatically rank as preservation expenses
options.explanation_md: An unrelated debt does not become a preservation cost merely because the customer owes it.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The provisions describe distinct rights; their statutory wording should not be collapsed into one universal retention rule.

payload.stem_md: A pledge agreement expressly limits the secured obligation and excludes later advances. A manager invokes the section 174 presumption to retain goods for a later advance without reading the exclusion. Which response fits the text?

options.text_md: The presumption necessarily overrides every contrary contractual term
options.explanation_md: The statutory presumption is qualified by the absence of anything to the contrary.

options.text_md: Section 174 eliminates the need to identify the debt for which goods were pledged
options.explanation_md: The provision makes that identification and any contract to a different effect relevant.

options.text_md: Read the contrary term before relying on the qualified subsequent-advance presumption
options.explanation_md: The express exclusion cannot be ignored by treating a qualified presumption as absolute.

options.text_md: Later advances automatically transfer full ownership of the goods to the lender
options.explanation_md: Retention as security is not an automatic transfer of full ownership.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The express exclusion cannot be ignored by treating a qualified presumption as absolute.
